os_version: macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), Apple Silicon, live user session
app: Java Swing (Tier F) on the JetBrains Runtime (OpenJDK 21.0.10) bundled with Android Studio. Re-run 2026-08-17 with a CONTROLLED probe after the first version's confound was caught. Cross-OS counterpart of windows-swing-jab and linux-java-swing-accessibility-api.

stack_detection.signature: Android Studio ships Contents/jbr (OpenJDK 21.0.10); the probe window is owned by a java process and answers AX directly — no bridge process, no jabswitch equivalent, no assistive-technology flag

channel_setup: Accessibility TCC only. STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE FROM BOTH OTHER OSes: there is no Java Access Bridge on macOS and none is needed — AWT's macOS peer maps Swing's AccessibleContext onto NSAccessibility itself. Windows needed JAB with an explicit -Djavax.accessibility flag and a full message pump; Linux needed the AtkWrapper assistive technology enabled and its jar on the classpath. On macOS the tree is simply there.

t1_read_text.detail: CORRECTION OF THE FIRST RUN, WHICH THIS CELL REPLACES. The first probe reported that Swing labels 'substitute' a name for their painted text and classified the cell silent. That result was an artifact of the probe itself: it called setAccessibleName() on every component. A controlled re-run puts both variants in one window — named and untouched — and the answer is unambiguous. UNTOUCHED components expose their painted text correctly in AXValue and AXDescription: 'SENTINEL-PLAIN bravo', 'countPlain=0', 'IncrementPlain' are all present and exact. Only the components whose accessibleName was explicitly overridden report the name instead, and there the painted text is genuinely unreachable in any attribute. So the channel faithfully relays what the application declares; the divergence was ours to cause. The residual, honest finding is an APP-ANNOTATION HAZARD rather than a channel defect: setAccessibleName on a JLabel makes its visible text unrecoverable through AX, which any app on any platform can do to itself. Worth a line in the paper, not a silent classification.

t2_enumerate.detail: RE-MEASURED 2026-08-17 on SwingProbe2.java itself (replication pass, Temurin 17) — the previous figures here ('10 nodes', an AXTextField) had been carried over from the retracted first probe, which this row now replaces. SwingProbe2's tree is 12 nodes: 5 AXStaticText, 5 AXButton (the two content buttons plus three window-chrome), 1 AXGroup, 1 AXWindow — correct roles throughout, and every node has usable geometry (12/12). Full walk 29.2 ms cold, 7.9 ms median warm over 5 runs; serialized view 198 bytes / 50 tokens. The cross-OS point is unchanged: Windows found UIA content-blind and had to bring up the Access Bridge, Linux had to enable AtkWrapper, and here the native tree answers with no setup at all.

t3_live_value.detail: SwingProbe2.java deliberately contains no JTextField, so this row is answered by a SEPARATE, explicitly-labelled test on SwingProbe.java (the first probe — valid for this purpose, since its confound concerned accessibleName substitution on labels, not field values). Measured 2026-08-17: the construction value is exposed (AXValue = 'initial'); then a unique string typed through layout-independent keycodes delivered with CGEventPostToPid reads back CHAR-EXACT via AXValue — 'REPL-T3-7Q42-café-naïve', accents intact, re-read 15.4 ms. Note the precise shape of the naming hazard: this field's accessibleName ('probe-field') lands in AXDescription while the LIVE VALUE stays in AXValue, so the t1 substitution hazard applies to a label's painted text, not to a text field's value.

t4_living_screen.detail: Untouched labels track their painted text, so a changing counter IS observable through the channel (countPlain reads its real value). The first run's claim to the contrary followed from the same confound and is withdrawn.

t5_blind_action.detail: THE FINDING THAT SURVIVED THE CONTROL, AND IT IS ON AN AXIS THE CAMPAIGN HAD NOT MEASURED. A Swing button — including one whose accessibility was never touched — declares NO actions at all: AXUIElementCopyActionNames returns an empty list. That declaration is honest and knowable a priori. But AXUIElementPerformAction(button, 'AXPress') then returns 0, i.e. SUCCESS, and nothing happens: six presses across two buttons, window raised and app frontmost, counters unchanged, confirmed on the window's own surface capture. kAXErrorActionUnsupported (-25206) exists precisely for this and is not used. So the ELEMENT is explicit while the PERFORM CALL fabricates success. A router that reads declarations is safe here; a router that trusts return codes is not — and trusting return codes is the default posture of every agent framework we know of.

t6_pictorial.detail: No pictorial region in the probe window.

measurements.notes: THE NEW AXIS: 'THE ACTION LIES ABOUT ITS EFFECT'. Every silent divergence found so far in this campaign was a bad READ — a view disagreeing with the screen. This is an ACT that reports success and does nothing, which is worse for an agent, because it proceeds believing the world moved and every subsequent step is reasoned from a false premise. It is also invisible to src/coverage-guard.mjs by construction: both guards inspect a VIEW, and nothing was wrong with the view. MITIGATION BUILT AND MEASURED, NOT JUST PROPOSED (campaign/macos/act_guard.py). The contract is channel-agnostic and applies equally to UIA Invoke(), AT-SPI do_action and CDP dispatchMouseEvent: read the target region's state, perform, then re-read; err != 0 is an EXPLICIT_FAILURE and should be believed, an unchanged state after a success return is UNVERIFIED, and only a changed state is CONFIRMED. Measured on both sides of the boundary in one session. The lying Swing button: declared_actions [], perform_err 0, state identical before and after -> UNVERIFIED, caught. The positive control, a native AppKit Calculator button: declared_actions ['AXPress'], perform_err 0, display changed -> CONFIRMED. No false alarm on the control, and the failure caught on the liar. COST, which is the reason this is practical: the structured re-read is 5 tokens on the Calculator and 38 on the Swing window, against 168 for a screenshot of that same small window — 4.4x to 34x cheaper than verifying with pixels, and the ratio widens with window size since the structured re-read scales with the affected region while a capture scales with the whole surface. Round-trip 507-517 ms, dominated by the deliberate repaint wait, not by the channel. TWO SIGNALS, USE BOTH: the empty action list is the free a-priori predictor (never call AXPress on an element that declares no actions — fall back to a synthetic click), and the state re-read is the runtime verification for when you do act. Neither alone is sufficient: the declaration does not tell you the press landed, and the verification costs a round-trip you can skip when the declaration already says no.

runtime_verification.method: Within-subject comparison of named vs untouched components in a single window; every string attribute of every node enumerated and searched for each painted string; six AXPress calls across both buttons with the app frontmost and the window raised; state read back through the channel and confirmed against the window's OWN surface capture (per the rule from macos-swiftui-thirdparty).
runtime_verification.agreement: Read side: exact for untouched components, and the mismatch on named ones is fully explained by the probe's own setAccessibleName call — no channel-caused divergence survives. Act side: channel returns success, screen unchanged, on both the named and the untouched button.

mitigation.module: act-guard (campaign/macos/act_guard.py) — the act-side counterpart of coverage-guard
mitigation.found_as: an action-side divergence (2026-08-17): AXUIElementPerformAction returns 0 = success on a Swing button that declares zero actions, while the application never sees the press
mitigation.trigger_signature: AXUIElementCopyActionNames returns an empty list, yet the element is an AXButton — free to check before acting; on any AWT/Swing process, treat perform return codes as unreliable
mitigation.result: guarded_act on the lying button returns UNVERIFIED (declared_actions [], err 0, state unchanged) and CONFIRMED on a native Calculator control (declared ['AXPress'], state changed); re-read costs 5-38 tokens vs 168 for a screenshot of the same window

permissions_required: Screen Recording for the window-surface verification
